speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help assess your infant's bilious vomiting and abdominal distension, was the baby born full-term, and have they had any bowel movements since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see that the infant is 2 days old, was born at home, and has not passed meconium. Has the infant had any episodes of bloody stool or signs of infection like fever?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Inability to pass meconium, Abdominal distension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Has the mother noticed any bloody mucousy stools, or has the infant had any signs of respiratory distress or failure to thrive? I will now order an abdominal X-ray to check for dilated bowel loops and a contrast enema to evaluate for a transition zone.

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray
REQUEST TEST: Contrast_Enema

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal_X-Ray: Dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, suggestive of a distal obstruction. Contrast_Enema: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal contrast enema is a crucial finding that helps narrow down the differential. I will now request a suction rectal biopsy to check for the presence of ganglion cells.

REQUEST TEST: Suction_Rectal_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Suction_Rectal_Biopsy: Absence of ganglion cells in the submucosa and myenteric plexus, consistent with Hirschsprung’s disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy confirms the absence of ganglion cells, which is diagnostic for Hirschsprung's disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease
